schema.description: Lists the image or video errors pertaining to transformation tasks in the last 3 days.

itemKind.description: The type of item returned, `LOGDETAILS` in this case.

items.description: A detailed list of the error details returned.
Lists image or video errors pertaining to transformation tasks.

actual.description: The actual value of the metric mentioned in the reason.

completeTime.description: Time when the transformation task completed.

pendingTime.description: Time when the transformation task was added to the queue. Present only when images or videos are queued for offline processing.

policyId.description: The ID of the policy used for an Image & Video Manager transformation.

reason.description: Provides a reason for an Image & Video Manager failure. The possible values are: `DURATION` when the pristine video exceeds the maximum duration of 5 minutes, `BYTES` when the pristine video exceeds the maximum size of 256 MB, `PIXEL` when the pristine video pixels exceed 3,686,400 (1920×1920), `SAMPLERATE` when the pristine video exceeds maximum sample rate of 60 Hz, `UNPARSEABLE` when the pristine video isn't a recognized or supported video format, `PRISTINE_TOO_WIDE` when the pristine image width exceeds 9999 pixels, `PRISTINE_TOO_TALL` when the pristine image height exceeds 9999 pixels, `PROCESS_FAILED_INTERNALLY` when the image or video couldn't be fetched from the origin or the policy is outdated, or `INVALID_POLICY` when the policy parameters are invalid.

size.description: The size breakpoint width in pixels configured in the policy.

startTime.description: Time when the transformation task execution started.

status.description: The status of the transformation task. The status is `PASSED` when the image or video processing succeeds, `FAILED`  when the image or video processing fails, or `QUEUED` when the image or video processing is queued for offline processing.

threshold.description: The threshold value of the metric mentioned in the reason.

transformationType.description: The type of transformation requested. The transformation type is `OFFLINE` if the image processing is queued for offline processing, or `REALTIME` if the image processing is performed in realtime.

totalItems.description: The total number of error records returned.

schema.description: Lists the policies for your configuration.

items.description: A detailed list of the policies returned.

oneOf.description: Specifies details for each policy, such as variations in image size and formats and the transformations to apply.
oneOf.title: Image policy

output.description: Dictates the output quality, either `quality` or `perceptualQuality`, and the formats created for each resized image. If unspecified, you get image formats that support all browsers at the default quality level of `85`, including WEBP, JPEG2000, and JPEG-XR for specific browsers.
output.title: Output

adaptiveQuality.description: Overrides the quality of the image to serve when Image & Video Manager detects a slow connection with a round-trip time (RTT) of less than 300 ms. Specifying lower values lets users with slow connections browse your site with reduced load times without impacting the quality of images for users with standard connections.

allowedFormats.description: The graphics file formats allowed for browser specific results, including `gif`, `jpeg`, `png`, `webp`, `jpegxr`, and `jpeg2000`.

items.description: The values of the allowed graphics file formats, including `gif`, `jpeg`, `png`, `webp`, `jpegxr`, and `jpeg2000`.

forcedFormats.description: The forced extra formats for the `imFormat` query parameter, which requests a specific browser type. By default, Image & Video Manager detects the browser and returns the appropriate image.

items.description: The values of the forced extra formats, including `gif`, `jpeg`, `png`, `webp`, `jpegxr`, and `jpeg2000`.

perceptualQuality.description: Mutually exclusive with `quality`. The perceptual quality to use when comparing resulting images, which overrides the `quality` setting. Perceptual quality tunes each image format's quality dynamically based on the human-perceived quality of the output image. This can result in greater byte savings as compared to using regular `quality` because many images can be encoded at a much lower quality without compromising the perceived quality of the image. In addition, certain images may need to be encoded at a slightly higher quality in order to maintain human-perceived quality. Value tiers are `high`, `mediumHigh`, `medium`, `mediumLow`, and `low`.

oneOf.description: References the name of a variable defined by the policy. Use this object to substitute preset values within transformations, or to pass in values dynamically using image URL query parameters.
oneOf.title: Inline variable

var.description: Corresponds to the `name` of the variable declared by the policy, to insert the corresponding value.

perceptualQualityFloor.description: Applies only when `perceptualQuality` is set. Sets a minimum image quality to respect when using perceptual quality. Perceptual quality won't reduce the quality below this value, even if it determines the compressed image to be acceptably visually similar.

quality.description: Mutually exclusive with `perceptualQuality`, used by default if neither is specified. The chosen quality of output images from 1-100, with 1 being the lowest quality and 100 being the highest.

oneOf.description: References the name of a variable defined by the policy. Use this object to substitute preset values within transformations, or to pass in values dynamically using image URL query parameters.
oneOf.title: Inline variable

var.description: Corresponds to the `name` of the variable declared by the policy, to insert the corresponding value.

postBreakpointTransformations.description: Post-processing Transformations are applied to the image after image and quality settings have been applied.

items.description: A transformation to apply to the image/object/text.

oneOf.title: BackgroundColor

color.description: The hexadecimal CSS color value for the background.

preserveMinorDimension.description: Whether to preserve the source image's minor dimension, `false` by default. The minor dimension is the dimension opposite the dimension that the appending `image` is placed. For example, the dimensions of the source image are 100 × 100 pixels. The dimensions of the appending `image` are 50 × 150 pixels. The `gravity` is set to `East`. This makes the major dimension horizontal and the source image's minor dimension vertical. To preserve the source image's minor dimension at 100 pixels, the `preserveMinorDimension` is set to `true`. As a result of the append, the major dimension expanded with the appended image to 150 pixels. The source image's minor dimension was maintained at 100 pixels. The total combined dimension of the image is 150 × 100 pixels.

Perceptual quality tunes each image format's quality dynamically based on the human-perceived quality of the output image. This can result in greater byte savings as compared to using regular `quality` because many images can be encoded at a much lower quality without compromising the perceived quality of the image. In addition, certain images may need to be encoded at a slightly higher quality in order to maintain human-perceived quality. Value tiers are `high`, `mediumHigh`, `medium`, `mediumLow`, and `low`.

This parameter strongly affects transformation performance. Be careful choosing values above the default if you expect to transform medium- to large-size images.

output.description: Dictates the output quality, either `quality` or `perceptualQuality`, and the formats created for each resized image. If unspecified, you get image formats that support all browsers at the default quality level of `85`, including WEBP, JPEG2000, and JPEG-XR for specific browsers.

adaptiveQuality.description: Overrides the quality of the image to serve when Image & Video Manager detects a slow connection with a round-trip time (RTT) of less than 300 ms. Specifying lower values lets users with slow connections browse your site with reduced load times without impacting the quality of images for users with standard connections.

allowedFormats.description: The graphics file formats allowed for browser specific results, including `gif`, `jpeg`, `png`, `webp`, `jpegxr`, and `jpeg2000`.

items.description: The values of the allowed graphics file formats, including `gif`, `jpeg`, `png`, `webp`, `jpegxr`, and `jpeg2000`.

forcedFormats.description: The forced extra formats for the `imFormat` query parameter, which requests a specific browser type. By default, Image & Video Manager detects the browser and returns the appropriate image.

items.description: The values of the forced extra formats, including `gif`, `jpeg`, `png`, `webp`, `jpegxr`, and `jpeg2000`.

perceptualQuality.description: Mutually exclusive with `quality`. The perceptual quality to use when comparing resulting images, which overrides the `quality` setting. Perceptual quality tunes each image format's quality dynamically based on the human-perceived quality of the output image. This can result in greater byte savings as compared to using regular `quality` because many images can be encoded at a much lower quality without compromising the perceived quality of the image. In addition, certain images may need to be encoded at a slightly higher quality in order to maintain human-perceived quality. Value tiers are `high`, `mediumHigh`, `medium`, `mediumLow`, and `low`.

This parameter strongly affects transformation performance. Be careful choosing values above the default if you expect to transform medium- to large-size images.

preserveMinorDimension.description: Whether to preserve the source image's minor dimension, `false` by default. The minor dimension is the dimension opposite the dimension that the appending `image` is placed. For example, the dimensions of the source image are 100 × 100 pixels. The dimensions of the appending `image` are 50 × 150 pixels. The `gravity` is set to `East`. This makes the major dimension horizontal and the source image's minor dimension vertical. To preserve the source image's minor dimension at 100 pixels, the `preserveMinorDimension` is set to `true`. As a result of the append, the major dimension expanded with the appended image to 150 pixels. The source image's minor dimension was maintained at 100 pixels. The total combined dimension of the image is 150 × 100 pixels.

density.description: Controls the density of control points used to distort the image. The largest dimension of the input image is divided up to fit this number of control points. This parameter strongly affects transformation performance. Be careful choosing values above the default if you expect to transform medium- to large-size images.

Perceptual quality tunes each image format's quality dynamically based on the human-perceived quality of the output image. This can result in greater byte savings as compared to using regular `quality` because many images can be encoded at a much lower quality without compromising the perceived quality of the image. In addition, certain images may need to be encoded at a slightly higher quality in order to maintain human-perceived quality. Value tiers are `high`, `mediumHigh`, `medium`, `mediumLow`, and `low`.

density.description: Controls the density of control points used to distort the image. The largest dimension of the input image is divided up to fit this number of control points. A grid of points is extended on the smaller dimension such that each row and column of control points is equidistant from each adjacent row or column. This parameter strongly affects transformation performance. Be careful choosing values above the default if you expect to transform medium- to large-size images.

preserveMinorDimension.description: Whether to preserve the source image's minor dimension, `false` by default. The minor dimension is the dimension opposite the dimension that the appending `image` is placed. For example, the dimensions of the source image are 100 × 100 pixels. The dimensions of the appending `image` are 50 × 150 pixels. The `gravity` is set to `East`. This makes the major dimension horizontal and the source image's minor dimension vertical. To preserve the source image's minor dimension at 100 pixels, the `preserveMinorDimension` is set to `true`. As a result of the append, the major dimension expanded with the appended image to 150 pixels. The source image's minor dimension was maintained at 100 pixels. The total combined dimension of the image is 150 × 100 pixels.

The minor dimension is the dimension opposite the dimension that the appending `image` is placed. For example, the dimensions of the source image are 100 × 100 pixels. The dimensions of the appending `image` are 50 × 150 pixels. The `gravity` is set to `East`. This makes the major dimension horizontal and the source image's minor dimension vertical. preserveMinorDimension.description: Whether to preserve the source image's minor dimension, `false` by default. The minor dimension is the dimension opposite the dimension that the appending `image` is placed. For example, the dimensions of the source image are 100 × 100 pixels. The dimensions of the appending `image` are 50 × 150 pixels. The `gravity` is set to `East`. This makes the major dimension horizontal and the source image's minor dimension vertical. To preserve the source image's minor dimension at 100 pixels, the `preserveMinorDimension` is set to `true`. As a result of the append, the major dimension expanded with the appended image to 150 pixels. The source image's minor dimension was maintained at 100 pixels. The total combined dimension of the image is 150 × 100 pixels.

density.description: Controls the density of control points used to distort the image. The largest dimension of the input image is divided up to fit this number of control points. This parameter strongly affects transformation performance. Be careful choosing values above the default if you expect to transform medium- to large-size images.

feather.description: The RemoveColor transformation may create a hard edge around an image. preserveMinorDimension.description: Whether to preserve the source image's minor dimension, `false` by default. The minor dimension is the dimension opposite the dimension that the appending `image` is placed. For example, the dimensions of the source image are 100 × 100 pixels. The dimensions of the appending `image` are 50 × 150 pixels. The `gravity` is set to `East`. This makes the major dimension horizontal and the source image's minor dimension vertical. To preserve the source image's minor dimension at 100 pixels, the `preserveMinorDimension` is set to `true`. As a result of the append, the major dimension expanded with the appended image to 150 pixels. The source image's minor dimension was maintained at 100 pixels. The total combined dimension of the image is 150 × 100 pixels.

perceptualQuality.description: Mutually exclusive with `quality`. The perceptual quality to use when comparing resulting images, which overrides the `quality` setting. Perceptual quality tunes each image format's quality dynamically based on the human-perceived quality of the output image. This can result in greater byte savings as compared to using regular `quality` because many images can be encoded at a much lower quality without compromising the perceived quality of the image. In addition, certain images may need to be encoded at a slightly higher quality in order to maintain human-perceived quality. Value tiers are `high`, `mediumHigh`, `medium`, `mediumLow`, and `low`.

preserveMinorDimension.description: Whether to preserve the source image's minor dimension, `false` by default. The minor dimension is the dimension opposite the dimension that the appending `image` is placed. For example, the dimensions of the source image are 100 × 100 pixels. The dimensions of the appending `image` are 50 × 150 pixels. The `gravity` is set to `East`. This makes the major dimension horizontal and the source image's minor dimension vertical. To preserve the source image's minor dimension at 100 pixels, the `preserveMinorDimension` is set to `true`. As a result of the append, the major dimension expanded with the appended image to 150 pixels. The source image's minor dimension was maintained at 100 pixels. The total combined dimension of the image is 150 × 100 pixels.
